title: Asking, inviting and saying no
goal: Ask for help without pushing, invite warmly, and say no without damaging the relationship: three things Sundanese culture handles with great care.

dialogs.title: Paguneman — Invited to a wedding
dialogs.intro: Bu Imas knocks on Rani's door holding a wedding invitation. Rani already has plans and has to decline without disappointing Bu Imas.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Néng, punten. Sabtu payun aya kondangan di tatangga.
lines.id: Néng, excuse me. Next Saturday there's a wedding party at the neighbors'.
lines.literal: Néng, excuse-me. Saturday next there-is wedding-party at neighbor.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Oh muhun, Bu. Aya naon acarana?
lines.id: Oh yes, ma'am. What's the occasion?
lines.literal: oh yes, Bu. there-is what event-the?

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Nikahan putrana Bu Éha. Hayu atuh ngiring sareng Ibu.
lines.id: Bu Éha's child is getting married. Come along with me!
lines.literal: wedding child-her Bu Éha. come-on [atuh] join with Ibu.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Aduh, Bu… Sabtu payun abdi aya acara kantor.
lines.id: Oh dear, ma'am… Next Saturday I have a work event.
lines.literal: oh-dear, Bu… Saturday next I there-is event office.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Tabuh sabaraha acarana? Kondangan mah ti tabuh sapuluh.
lines.id: What time is it? The wedding party starts at ten.
lines.literal: hour how-many event-the? wedding-party [mah] from hour ten.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Ti énjing dugi ka soré, Bu. Hapunten pisan.
lines.id: From morning till late afternoon, ma'am. I'm so sorry.
lines.literal: from morning until to afternoon, Bu. sorry very.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Nya teu nanaon atuh. Damel mah kedah didahulukeun.
lines.id: Oh, that's fine. Work comes first.
lines.literal: yes no what-what [atuh]. work [mah] must be-put-first.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Punten, tiasa nyuhunkeun tulung teu, Bu?
lines.id: Excuse me, could I ask you a favor, ma'am?
lines.literal: excuse-me, can request help not, Bu?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Upami kenging, titip amplop kanggo Bu Éha. Sareng punten kanggo abdi.
lines.id: If it's all right, could you take an envelope to Bu Éha for me? And pass on my apologies.
lines.literal: if allowed, entrust envelope for Bu Éha. and excuse-me for me.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Tangtos. Engké ku Ibu dipasihkeun. Bu Éha ogé ngartos pasti.
lines.id: Of course. I'll give it to her. Bu Éha will understand, I'm sure.
lines.literal: certainly. later by Ibu given. Bu Éha also understand surely.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Hatur nuhun pisan, Bu. Punten ngarepotkeun.
lines.id: Thank you so much, ma'am. Sorry to trouble you.
lines.literal: thank you very, Bu. excuse-me troubling.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Ulah sungkan-sungkan. Urang mah geus kaya kulawarga.
lines.id: Don't feel awkward about it. We're like family now.
lines.literal: don't hesitant-hesitant. we [mah] already like family.

notes: **Ngiring** = to come along, join (lemes); loma: **milu**. *Hayu ngiring* = come along. It's also used for sharing a feeling: *ngiring bingah* = I share your joy (congratulations).
**Kondangan** = to attend a celebration, especially a wedding. An older Sundanese word: **nyaba** or **ngahadiran**.
**Didahulukeun** comes from *dahulu* (first) + *di-…-keun*: "be put first." *Damel mah kedah didahulukeun* is Bu Imas's way of releasing Rani from feeling guilty, a very typical social move.
**Titip** = to leave something with someone to pass on. *Titip amplop* at a wedding means sending your gift of money without attending, which is common and not seen as rude.
**Tangtos** = of course, certainly (lemes); loma: **tangtu**. A warmer answer to a favor than *muhun*.

**Sungkan** = hesitant, reluctant out of politeness or awkwardness. *Ulah sungkan-sungkan* = don't feel awkward. This word explains a lot of Sundanese behavior: many requests go unspoken out of *sungkan*, which is why offering first is so appreciated.

grammars.title: Asking and forbidding
body: Sundanese doesn't have a special command form of the verb. A command is just the base word, softened by an opening word or a particle.
after: ⚠️ **Ulah** and **entong** both mean "don't." *Ulah* is standard and safe anywhere; *entong* feels more relaxed and is often used with children and close friends.
When asking someone you respect, the passive actually sounds more polite than the active. *Mangga dicandak* (please, have it taken) is gentler than *mangga nyandak* (please take it).
The safest opener for any request: **Punten, tiasa nyuhunkeun tulung teu?** It asks permission to ask, which gives the other person an easy way out if they can't help right now.

blocks.title: Inviting
items: **Hayu urang ka ____.** — Let's go to ____. (loma)
**Mangga ngiring sareng abdi.** — Please come along with me. (lemes)
**Hayu atuh, sakedap waé.** — Oh, come on, just for a bit.
**Kersa henteu ngiring?** — Would you like to come along?
**Engké urang bareng.** — We'll go together later.
**Ditunggu nya di ditu.** — We'll be waiting for you there.

blocks.title: Accepting an invitation
items: **Hayu!** — Let's go!
**Mangga atuh.** — All right then.
**Tangtos, hatur nuhun tos diajak.** — Of course, thanks for inviting me.
**Insya Allah abdi ngiring.** — God willing, I'll come.
**Sip, engké abdi ka ditu.** — Great, I'll be there later.
**Kabeneran abdi teu aya acara.** — As it happens, I'm free.

blocks.text: Saying no is the most delicate social skill in Sundanese, and it almost always follows the same order: **apologize, give a reason, offer something instead**. Skip any one part and the refusal feels cold.

head: Part
Sentence
English
rows: I'll join you later once it's over.
Please give Bu Éha my regards.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Insya Allah** (God willing) and **engké abdi wartosan deui** (I'll let you know) often work as a gentle no, not a promise. It isn't dishonesty; it's a way of saving face on both sides. As a newcomer you need to do two things: **recognize** it when you hear it, and **don't use it** if you really do mean to come. In that case answer clearly: *muhun, abdi ngiring*.

blocks.title: Ways to say no
items: **Hapunten pisan, abdi teu tiasa.** — I'm so sorry, I can't.
**Aya acara sanés, Bu.** — I have something else on, ma'am.
**Sanés teu daék, ngan leres teu tiasa.** — It's not that I don't want to, I really can't.
**Kapan-kapan waé nya.** — Another time, okay?
**Engké abdi nyusul upami rengse.** — I'll join you later once it's over.
**Titip salam waé kanggo anjeunna.** — Please give him/her my regards.

blocks.title: Asking for help
items: **Punten, tiasa nyuhunkeun tulung teu?** — Excuse me, could I ask a favor?
**Tulung candakkeun ____.** — Could you get me ____, please?
**Upami kenging, titip ____.** — If it's all right, could you take ____ for me?
**Punten ngarepotkeun.** — Sorry for the trouble.
**Teu kedah upami repot.** — Don't worry if it's too much trouble.
**Hatur nuhun pisan tos dibantosan.** — Thank you so much for your help.
